title: Contracted throughput negotiator and safety budgeting for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers can purchase contracted throughput (committed tokens/sec) for predictable billing and performance. Today we rely on simple headroom heuristics and global burst credits; customers have requested stronger contractual guarantees with predictable safety behavior during demand spikes and infra flaps.

Goal:
Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine component (the 'Throughput Negotiator') that: (1) translates per-tenant contracted throughput into target metrics for the allocator, (2) enforces conservative scaling with explicit safety budgets (debt and rollback windows), and (3) exposes deterministic behaviors for billing and SLOs.

High-level approach:
- Target metric composition: compute a per-tenant scaling target as a composite metric that blends observed sustained token throughput, 95th/99th latency percentiles for generated sequences, and reserved contracted throughput. The negotiated target is the max of (contracted throughput, sustained demand * headroom_factor) but subject to safety caps.
- Scaling algorithm: hybrid approach combining a demand-tracking leaky-bucket (for short bursts) with a conservative PI-like controller for capacity adjustments. The leaky-bucket allows controlled short-duration overshoot; the controller adjusts replica counts based on smoothed error between negotiated target and observed throughput.
- Safety limits: explicit parameters for max ramp per minute (ramp_limit_pct), maximum burst debt (debt_tokens or debt_seconds), cool-down window after scale-up/scale-down, and a rollback window with automated graceful degradation (fallback to lower-cost model variant or rate-limit).

Components to implement:
- Negotiator service (stateless controller) that computes per-tenant targets and issues desired_capacity signals to Fleet Orchestrator.
- Debt accounting store (time-series entries per tenant) to track consumed burst budget and decay schedule. Implemented as an append-only time series with TTL and efficient rollup.
- Policy DSL extension: new config keys for contracted_throughput, headroom_factor, ramp_limit_pct, max_burst_debt, cooloff_seconds, rollback_policy. Provide new JSON/YAML schema and validation.
- Metrics/telemetry hooks: expose negotiated_target, observed_throughput, debt_balance, last_scale_action, and circuit_state for each tenant.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Conservative default safety values to prioritize availability and predictable billing over aggressive scaling. Customers can opt into aggressive profiles via dedicated contracts.
- Debt model vs. token-bucket: debt accounting is chosen to give transparent 'borrowed capacity' semantics tied to billing and entitlement.
- Controller frequency: reconcile every 15s for responsiveness, with rate-limits on replica churn to avoid oscillation.

Example policy snippet (YAML):
policy: |
  tenant_policy: 
    contracted_throughput: 1200  # tokens/sec guaranteed in contract
    headroom_factor: 1.25        # scale target = max(contracted, sustained*1.25)
    ramp_limit_pct: 20          # max change in capacity per minute
    max_burst_debt: 30000       # tokens allowed to borrow in a 1h window
    cooloff_seconds: 300        # cooldown after any scale event
    rollback_policy: graceful-fallback

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): implement negotiator + test harness, run against synthetic tenants in staging using recorded production traffic patterns.
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable feature for a small set of committed customers with explicit contract fields and guardrails; observe debt consumption and circuit transitions.
- Phase 3 (GA): document billing impact, expose UI toggles in Console, publish migration notes for Dedicated customers.

Metrics to validate success:
- SLA adherence: % time tenants meet contracted_throughput during business hours (target > 99.5% for committed customers).
- Paging incidents due to scaling oscillation: target < 1 per month for pilot tenants.
- Cost delta: median cost per contracted token should not increase by > 5% after default policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Negotiator computes and publishes negotiated_target for each tenant and reconciles capacity signals within configured cooloff windows.
- Debt accounting correctly charges and decays borrowed capacity; debt_balance exposed in metrics and logs.
- Safety limits (ramp_limit_pct, max_burst_debt) are enforced and tested by chaos scenarios (node loss, sudden spike).
- New policy config validated by API and error messages surfaced in Console when invalid.
- End-to-end integration tests in staging with synthetic spikes and failovers demonstrate no uncontrolled replica thrashing.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator publishes per-tenant negotiated_target and desired_capacity within 15s of reconciliation.
Debt accounting records borrow and decay behavior; debt_balance metric matches simulated consumption in tests.
Ramp limits prevent > configured percent capacity change per minute during stress tests.
Rollback policy triggers during sustained infra shortfall and produces expected fallback actions (model downgrade or rate-limit).
Console shows policy validation errors and tenant debt metrics for pilot customers.

Implement Negotiator service and debt accounting store
Add metrics and tracing hooks; update Console telemetry pages
